# The provenance file on Tfnt

*Catalogue entry — Tfnt. Every claim below carries its chain of custody.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **𓏏𓆑𓈖𓏏𓁐**, from the tradition's own record. On record: Heliopolitan and Memphite cosmogonies, Book of the Heavenly Cow (Destruction of Mankind), Leiden Papyrus I 384 (Return of the Eye), Pyramid Texts (Shu–Tefnut pair).

**2. The narrative record.** **The Spat-Forth Pair** — In the Memphite and Heliopolitan accounts the creator — Atum or Ra — produced his first two children by spitting (tf) and sneezing: Tefnut the moisture and Shu the air.  Their names are the verbs of that first physiology; the world’s atmosphere is the afterbirth of the god’s own body. **The Flight to Nubia** — When the creator grew old, men plotted against him — and his Eye, sent to punish them, abandoned her post in fury and fled south as a raging lioness.  Egypt withered without her.

**3. The physical record.** She appears with Shu flanking the solar barque in tomb and temple programmes from the Old Kingdom onward — the twin supports of the sun’s journey. Fine lioness-headed examples survive in the Ramesside temples of the Theban west bank and in the Louvre’s statuary of the solar triads.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/tefnut/](/tefnut/), a temple of the restored name. aSCII-equivalent form

**5. The documented resonances.** **Freshwater & Hydrology**, **Agriculture, Food & Harvest**, **Meteorology & Weather Intelligence** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/tefnut/blog/resonance/).

**6. The primary sources.** [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**7. The continuing record.** The spit-and-sneeze cosmogony remains a favourite exhibit of Egyptian theology’s concreteness — the first act of creation as a bodily reflex.  Her lioness form fed the iconography of Egyptian goddesses generally; and the Leiden ‘Return of the Eye’ is a set text of Middle Egyptian literature courses for its perfect rhetoric.
